title: Glucosyl Extraction from Glycogen by Acid Hydrolysis
author: Daniel T Hass

steps.title: Prepare all required buffers
steps.instruction: Make extraction buffer (80 % methanol, 20 % ethanol) at a minimum volume of 1.5 mL per sample; if the extract will be used for mass spectrometry, use HPLC‑grade solvents and add the appropriate internal standard. Prepare hydrolysis buffer as 2 N HCl in water. Prepare neutralization buffer as 2 N ammonium bicarbonate (NH₄OCOOH) in water.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer and homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer flash‑frozen tissue stored at –80 °C to dry ice, add 500 µL extraction buffer to each 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, and homogenize using a method suitable for the tissue. For mouse retina, use an ultrasonic homogenizer at 10 % of maximum power output, applying 10 pulses (each pulse is a duty cycle). Apply the same settings for RPE‑choroid‑sclera tissue.

steps.title: Centrifuge to collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenized sample at 17,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C. Transfer the supernatant, which contains free glucose and other metabolites, to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Wash pellet with extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the protein/glycogen pellet in 500 µL fresh extraction buffer, vortex, and repeat the centrifugation step (17,000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C). Perform this wash a second time (total of three extractions). Combine all supernatants, dry if desired, and keep the final pellet for hydrolysis.

steps.title: Acid hydrolysis of glycogen
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, resuspend the washed pellet in 50–100 µL 2 N HCl hydrolysis buffer, seal the tube securely, and incubate at 80 °C for 1 hour using a heat block or water bath.

steps.title: Neutralize hydrolysate
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from heat and add, dropwise, an equal volume of 2 N NH₄OCOOH neutralization buffer. Vortex the mixture and centrifuge at 17,000 × g (time not specified) to pellet large debris. Note that the reaction will bubble; add the base slowly to avoid overflow.

steps.title: Collect glucosyl‑containing supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared supernatant to a new tube; this contains the glucose monomers derived from glycogen and can be analyzed enzymatically or by mass spectrometry.

steps.title: Optional LC‑MS sample clean‑up
steps.instruction: If the sample will be injected directly onto an LC‑MS column, dry the supernatant, re‑constitute in 90 % methanol, vortex, then pellet at 17,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Transfer the methanol supernatant to a fresh tube; salts remain in the pellet while glucose stays largely in the supernatant (note that glucose recovery has not been formally tested).

description: Incubate tissue extract on dry ice for >45 minutes. Notes : Proteins and glycogen should be poorly soluble in methanol/ethanol and should precipitate
